v1.19.2-palette.4 — Profiles, a new tab page, and no AI

### What's new
- **Switch browser profile** (`gP`, `:profile`, or *Switch Profile…* in the palette): lists the browser's profiles; picking one brings that profile's window forward with a new tab, or opens one. Needs the native messaging host (neovim) — see [src/nvim/server/Readme.md](https://github.com/hoangtrung99/Surfingkeys/blob/master/src/nvim/server/Readme.md). Chromium-based browsers on macOS and Linux.
- **Tabs of your other profiles in the palette** (`Ctrl/⌘+Shift+P`): each other open profile of the same browser shows as a *Tabs in &lt;profile&gt;* group; Enter switches to that tab and its window. Also through the native host; tab titles and addresses pass between the profiles over a local socket only and are never written to disk.
- **New tab page** (`pages/newtab.html`): your bookmarks bar (folders as dropdowns) and top sites, with the keyboard already in the page so Surfingkeys' keys work at once. In Helium, set `helium://flags/#custom-ntp` to `chrome-extension://aajlcoiaogpknhgninhopncaldipjdnp/pages/newtab.html` and relaunch.
- The **Auto** theme now follows the system on the popup, the help page and the new tab page.

### Removed
- **The AI features**: the `A` chat, translation with `;t`, `;lt` and visual `t`, and grammar correction with `Ctrl-g` in insert mode. `settings.llm` is ignored. AI settings saved by earlier versions are left as they are; *Reset settings* clears them.

### Fixes
- Native host: a neovim config can no longer write into the host's messaging pipe, and the neovim page says why neovim is unavailable.

### Install
1. Download `surfingkeys-palette-v1.19.2-palette.4.zip` below and unzip it.
2. Open `chrome://extensions` and turn on **Developer mode**.
3. Click **Load unpacked** and pick the unzipped folder (or replace the folder of an existing install and click **Reload**; settings are kept).
4. For `gP` and other profiles' tabs, install the native host as described in `src/nvim/server/Readme.md`.
